entries.subject: Vilenius et al. (2018) two-chord occultation reanalysis
entries.finding: The selected source is the published timing-error reanalysis and its conditional a/c about 1.3 ellipsoidal example: the displayed projected ellipse is 363 x 289 km with an effective diameter of 323 (+95/-37) km, and the illustration assumes a 363 km equatorial depth.

entries.subject: Older 2010 circular 286 km occultation fit
entries.finding: The README records that the old 2010 circular fit was affected by a timing offset and is not treated as definitive; the selected 2018 publication retains broad size uncertainty instead.
entries.revisitWhen: A new occultation or reanalysis restores a circular solution or supersedes the 2018 timing-error reanalysis.

entries.subject: Uniqueness of the three-dimensional shape
entries.finding: Only two chords were observed, which the README says do not uniquely determine the shape, so the axisymmetric depth is assumed rather than measured.
entries.revisitWhen: A multi-chord occultation or resolved imaging determines the third axis.

entries.subject: cssEarth missing-coverage grid as the surface
entries.finding: No surface imagery exists for this body, so the manifest supplies the project-authored missing-coverage grid, the normal grid marks unmapped terrain and Shadows defaults off.

entries.subject: Water-ice spectral evidence and high albedo as a surface map
entries.finding: The README records that the water-ice spectra and high albedo describe unresolved surface composition, not a spatially resolved ice map, so the standard grid remains in place of a texture.
entries.revisitWhen: A spatially resolved composition or albedo map of 2002 TX300 is published.
